title: Daler Mehndi thanks fans for their support during Uttarakhand event controversy, says brother Mika Singh showed up like a force to reckon with
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Punjabi singer Daler Mehndi made headlines after Uttarakhand Cabinet Minister Subodh Uniyal reprimanded him on stage during a cultural evening and questioned his conduct, alleging that he was intoxicated. Mika Singh had called on Uttarakhand minister Subodh Uniyal to apologise. After weeks since the incident, Daler has finally broken his silence on this row and rolled out a statement on his Instagram account.

Adding to this, Daler Mehndi has spoken out on the entire row that erupted last month over his live performance. Daler's note He wrote, "Over the years, I have received so much love through my music and on every stage I have stood. But what I have experienced of late has touched me in a way that is difficult to put into words. The way you stood by me, the way you spoke for me, the faith you showed in me and the love you gave me I don’t think I can ever fully express what it has meant to me."

Meanwhile, Daler did not miss a special mention for his brother and singer Mika Singh , and wrote, “My family has been my greatest strength through this time. My brother Mika stood up for me like a force to reckon with.” He thanked his family and all other members of the entertainment industry for showing support.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Daler Mehndi (@thedalermehndiofficial)

As per the latest buzz, Daler shared that he felt fortunate to have felt so much love for him in this lifetime and that he will never forget the kindness. He concluded his note by extending his wishes for Diwali.

In further updates, Singer Daler Mehndi performed at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in New Tehri, Uttarakhand, on Sunday night. He was interrupted mid-performance and reprimanded on stage by Uttarakhand Cabinet Minister Subodh Uniyal. The minister criticised the singer's conduct and shared, “You cannot even speak, so how are you going to sing?”, hinting that the singer was intoxicated. The clip subsequently circulated widely on social media.

On top of that, Later, while in conversation with ANI, Subodh explained why he had reprimanded Daler publicly. He shared, “He is a big artist. If a big artist doesn't do justice to their art... He seemed disoriented on stage and didn't seem to be able to even keep standing. Besides this, he was only lip-syncing to his songs. I told him that he is a big artist and he should do justice to his art; he had been offered ₹ 35 lakh to come and perform, but he was not even singing. So, I expressed my resentment."

Following the incident, Daler's brother and fellow singer Mika Singh, along with several other celebrities, criticised the minister for disrespecting the singer. Mika also shared that Daler was unwell during the performance.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 4 (updated live): Diwali boost propels Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi film past ₹200 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana seems to be recovering after a good, but not great, start at the domestic ticket-window. The most expensive Indian movie ever made set a new record for a pre-Diwali rollout in India. But there were concerns about its earnings on the day of the festival. However, on Sunday, the movie allayed all those fears to register an all-time record for Diwali

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor and Yash play Rama and Ravana, respectively, in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Ramayana ticket-window update Ramayana began with houseful shows on day 1, netting ₹ 64.85 crore rupees net in India on its opening day. The figure was low given the movie’s scale, but it was still the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. On Friday, Ramayana fell slightly, bringing in ₹ 48 crore rupees, but jumped up on Saturday to mint almost ₹ 70 crore rupees net. This took its three-day domestic haul to an impressive ₹ 183 crore rupees net. On Sunday, despite Diwali keeping footfalls low in part of the country, Ramayana had a great day. The movie collected ₹ 32 crore rupees net in India by 5 PM, taking its earnings past ₹ 200 crore rupees in just four days. Its domestic haul now stands at a formidable ₹ 215 crore rupees .

Meanwhile, What is worrisome for the movie is that its earnings have come largely on the back of some good performance by the Hindi version. Despite Yash’s presence as Ravana, the Kannada version has started extremely slowly. It collected just ₹ 7.50 crore rupees on day 1 and has lacked pace since. Of the other versions, Telugu has fared well, while Malayalam and Tamil are just filling the ranks.

Notably, While the Diwali weekend has seen many big films rolled out in theatres over the years, very few rollout on the day of the festival itself, choosing to maximise the days after Diwali. But Ramayana came out three days before it, which meant its biggest day - the first Sunday - falls on Diwali. It is currently tracking to beat Tiger 3’s all-time Diwali earnings record. The Salman Khan-starrer collected �� 44.50 crore rupees in net ticket-window on Diwali 2023. Ramayana is aiming for a ₹ 60+ crore rupees day as things stand currently.

As per the latest buzz, On its opening day, Ramayana beat the opening-day hauls of blockbusters such as Pathaan ( ₹ 57 crore rupees), Animal ( ₹ 63 crore rupees), and Drishyam 2 ( ₹ 62 crore rupees). But it fell short of Adipurush, the previous adaptation of the epic that opened at ₹ 86.75 crore rupees. The trend continued on the second and third days. But thanks to its extended weekend, Ramayana managed to surpass the Prabhas-starrer on day 4. Adipurush collected ₹ 237 crore rupees net in India in its first four days. Ramayana is almost certain to cross the mark by the end of Sunday.

In further updates, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kareena Kapoor Khan (@kareenakapoorkhan)

Notably, Kareena is the daughter of actors Randhir Kapoor and Babita and the granddaughter of Raj Kapoor. Her elder sister Karisma Kapoor is also an star. Kareena is married to Saif Ali Khan and the couple have two sons – Taimur and Jehangir, aka Jeh.

As per the latest buzz, The star keeps posting pictures of her sons during festivals and family get togethers. Kareena, spoke about her family roots in an interview with Ranveer Allahabadia on BeerBiceps podcast and shared, “My mother (Babita) came from a very middle-class family. My nana (Hari Shivdasani) was also an star but we were never made to feel like we come from this filmy family. The first time I went on a set was when I was 8 or 9 years old when Chintu uncle was shooting in Kashmir with Rekha ji. In those days my grandfather (Raj Kapoor) was also very relaxed. Nobody felt that they were very big stars. They were very passionate about arts and culture.”

In further updates, Kareena returned with her chat show What Women Want. She was also seen in an episode of Koffee with Karan with Saif. There, the couple spoke in detail about the horrific knife attack on Saif at their home last year, breaking their silence on the conspiracies on whether it was staged and how the star recovered so quickly. Recalling the ordeal, Saif called it “the worst night in the history of nights.” The star opened up about the severity of his injuries and the strength it took to remain composed through the situation, especially with their children witnessing it. “You could not walk!” Kareena recalled, sharing how the doctor had to move his nerves to take out the knife from his spine. “I was a wreck, he was fine,” she shared. Kareena shared their youngest son, Jeh, saw the entire incident with his own eyes and gifted Saif his plastic sword to protect him in the future. “He thinks of Saif as some sort of Iron Man,” shared Kareena.

On top of that, Meanwhile, on the acting front, Kareena was of late seen headlining investigative drama Daayra. The movie stars Kareena and Prithviraj Sukumaran as cops who face off while navigating the dark and complex world of juvenile crime.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The couple introduced the 19-year-old as he begins his musical journey with a short movie titled Slide. In their social media post, they looked back at his growing years, recalling how the once-shy child who would hesitate to sing in front of his father has slowly grown into a young artist willing to put in the hours to pursue his passion.

Adding to this, nu Nigam's son Nevaan steps into music world with short movie Slide. Sonu Nigam shares son's journey into music In their note, Sonu and Madhurima looked back at Nevaan's journey from childhood to the young musician he is today. They recalled how he once hesitated to sing in front of his father and spoke about the dedication he has shown towards music over the years.

Meanwhile, Sonu shared a photo and wrote, “On this auspicious and pious occasion of Diwali, Nevaan embarks upon his journey into the world of Music venturing into a path far flung from his Grandfather and Father to explore his own horizons. From a chubby little boy to a fit and lean young man, from someone who was extremely shy to sing in front of his own father, to someone who's practicing the vocal exercises taught to him by his brilliant vocal coach 16 hours a day and cracking one take recordings in the studio with the legend Poo Bear, from someone who had a tough time jogging even for merely 3 minutes, to someone who's doing hours of dance practise to hone his skills; Nevaan has truly made our family very very thankful and happy, (Proud, is a word I avoid using in life)!”

title: Amitabh Bachchan says he is facing discomfort in writing letters to thank fans for their gifts, extends them wishes on Diwali
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Amitabh Bachchan told followers last month that he will take a break from his usual social media updates after being advised to rest and recover. The 84-year-old star has been busy shooting for Kaun Banega Crorepati as a host as well as the sequel to Kalki 2898 AD. On the occasion of Diwali, the veteran star put a new post on his Tumblr account to speak about his current health situation and also extended wishes to everyone on the occasion of Diwali.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan has spoken about his current health situation. What Amitabh wrote Starting his post with good wishes to his followers and well-wishers for a happy Diwali, Amitabh wrote, "I have been receiving greetings and gifts from so many well-wishers, and in such abundance that I am now running out of space to keep them. Not storing these gifts properly would amount to disrespecting them. Therefore, to all of you who have been sending gifts as expressions of your affection, I wish to convey my appreciation and acknowledgement. I am also making an effort to respond to each of you personally through letters.”

Meanwhile, "I really wanted to write these replies myself. However, I have been experiencing some discomfort in the hand, for writing, which has caused delay. I sincerely apologise (folded hands emoji),” added the star.

Notably, He also shared, “But what can one do? Circumstances have become such that apologising seems to come easily. One should seek forgiveness. After all, there is nothing wrong with asking for it. The other person may refuse, reject the apology, or understand and accept it. If they understand and accept the apology, my heart will be filled with happiness. If they do not, their mind will remain troubled.”

As per the latest buzz, The message followed a similar update on his personal blog while extending his Dussehra wishes last month. The star had shared in a previous blog post that he had been given strict instructions to focus on his recovery and avoid communication for the time being. "First Dussehra greetings to all .. love happiness, fulfilment, prayers. Under very strict rest and recuperation .. so am not allowed to communicate .. do excuse .. my apologies," he wrote. He also added, “But do take this as my respected response .. more hopefully later.”

In further updates, A bomb threat email targeting Amitabh Bachchan's bungalow, the Bombay High Court and Mumbai's Mahalaxmi Racecourse prompted security agencies to launch an investigation on Friday. Authorities later verified the threat to be a hoax.

On top of that, Amitabh's message also comes as the police investigate the firing incident involving Tiger Shroff's car. Reports about the case suggest that the suspects had allegedly surveyed other prominent personalities before deciding on their target. According to several reports, the accused had considered the residences of Amitabh Bachchan, Akshay Kumar and Aamir Khan. However, they as per reports dropped the idea after assessing the security arrangements around the actors' homes.

On the work front, he is set to return in the sequel to Nag Ashwin's science-fiction movie Kalki 2898 AD, which stars Prabhas and Kamal Haasan . On television, the star continues to host the 18th season of Kaun Banega Crorepati, the long-running quiz show closely associated with him.

body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

AICC general secretary K C Venugopal on Sunday shared the Congress-led agitation against CEC Gyanesh Kumar would continue until he was removed from the post and the country's electoral system was made impartial and transparent.

Adding to this, Venugopal alleged that the deletion of names from electoral rolls would deprive poor people of their voting rights and access to various government benefits. (File Photo/ANI) In conversation with reporters here, Venugopal shared protests were continuing across states and districts, with only a brief pause expected during the Diwali festival.

Meanwhile, He described the November 1 rally organised by the Congress in New Delhi as one of the strongest protests witnessed in the country, saying the party was fighting against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

Notably, "We will withdraw from this agitation only after Gyanesh Kumar is removed from the post and steps are taken to make India's electoral system and processes flawless, impartial and fair. This is not a struggle that we will abandon midway," he shared.

As per the latest buzz, Venugopal alleged that the deletion of names from electoral rolls would deprive poor people of their voting rights and access to various government benefits, which, he claimed, were increasingly being linked to voter identity cards.
In further updates, He shared the Congress would launch a nationwide 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' (Save the Vote, Save the Nation) campaign at the panchayat level over the next one-and-a-half months.

On top of that, As part of the campaign, the party would appoint a 'Vote Rakshak' (guardian) in every polling booth to scrutinise electoral rolls, identify people whose names had been deleted and visit their homes to help them get their names restored, he shared.
Congress units were organising programmes across states and districts, while plans were also being drawn up for joint programmes with other political parties, he shared.

title: 'Mockery of democracy': Ex-BJP MP Gopal Shetty tonsures head in protest over BMC demolition in Borivali
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Former BJP MP Gopal Shetty has tonsured his head in protest against the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's (BMC) demolition of 27 houses in Borivali East, alleging that the civic body acted in haste without giving residents time to retrieve their belongings.

Adding to this, Former BJP MP Gopal Shetty stagng a protest against the BMC's demolition drive at Borivali in Mumbai, following the demolition of an unauthorised structure on a reserved plot. (Hindustan Times/File) Calling the sudden early-morning drive on November 4 a "mockery of democracy", Shetty on Saturday claimed the structures stood on private land occupied for nearly 50 years, and criticized the local BJP leadership for not supporting the affected families.

Meanwhile, The BMC demolished 27 houses built on a 3,400-sq-metre plot, reserved for a BEST bus station, on Swami Vivekanand Road in Borivali East. The drive was carried out after the Supreme Court pulled up the civic body for failing to remove encroachments despite earlier directions.

Notably, The court had also ordered a freeze on the November salaries of Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide and concerned officials, besides initiating contempt proceedings. It subsequently withdrew the salary-related direction and contempt notice after the BMC informed it that the structures had been removed.

As per the latest buzz, In conversation with reporters, the BJP leader shared he had tonsured his head as a mark of protest as the affected families were not allowed to remove their household belongings before the demolition.

In further updates, "I have never seen such action in my public life. Even a person like (26/11 terror attack) Ajmal Kasab was given eight years to face trial and an opportunity to approach the President after his conviction," he shared.
On top of that, He claimed that residents were given notices around 1.30 am and their houses were demolished by 7 am, without allowing them sufficient time to remove their belongings.

He further questioned the manner in which the civic body presented the matter before the apex court, accusing it of failing to submit copies of notices issued to occupants and their replies, as sought by the court.

title: HT Exclusive: Vinod Kapri on casting an 80-year-old Army veteran and a 70-year-old woman with no acting experience as Pyre's elderly lead couple
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

National Award-winning filmmaker Vinod Kapri 's search for the lead actors of Pyre took several years, countless auditions and a few unexpected turns. He had considered actors such as Naseeruddin Shah and Ratna Pathak Shah, and even tried making the movie with the real-life couple who inspired the story. But the faces he was looking for eventually came from two rather unexpected places.

Adding to this, Vinod Kapri's Pyre features Padam Singh Kapri, 80, and Heera Devi, 70, both first-time actors from Uttarakhand. Set in Uttarakhand's Kumaon region, Pyre tells the story of an elderly couple whose children have left their village in search of better opportunities. With no one else around, the two are left to navigate old age, loneliness and the changing life of their mountain home. The movie looks at migration through the lives of parents who stay behind while the younger generation moves away.

Meanwhile, Pyre features Padam Singh Kapri, 80, and Heera Devi, 70, both first-time actors from Uttarakhand. Padam, a retired Indian Army serviceman, plays a character named after himself, while Heera takes on the role of Tulsi. The movie has won 18 international awards and is produced by Vinod Kapri, Suresh Joshi and Arindra Rai Chaudhuri under Bhagirathi Films and Mashakbeen Studios. It rolled out in theatres across India on October 30 in Hindi and Malayalam.

Notably, In conversation with Hindustan Times, Vinod looked back at the unusual journey that brought his two lead actors on board. One was discovered during his father's 80th birthday celebration, while the other came into the picture during a stop on a village road.

As per the latest buzz, The idea for Pyre took shape in 2018, when Vinod met an elderly couple in Munsyari, Uttarakhand. He spent close to two hours talking to them and recorded their conversation on his phone. Their bond left a lasting impression on him, and he initially felt they should play themselves in the movie. He even spent eight to 10 days shooting with them, hoping to bring their story to the screen. However, the experience soon made him realise that their real-life chemistry alone was not enough to carry the movie.

In further updates, "That was my first attempt to make this movie with them and but I failed miserably because we went there unprepared and they don't even understand they don't have even understanding of cinema or camera or acting or anything. I realized that should look for more mature actors," he shared.

On top of that, Vinod then began searching for elderly actors from the Himalayan region who could bring a natural understanding of the setting, its culture and language to the story. He auditioned more than 50 to 60 people over the next two years, but none seemed right for the roles. After struggling to find his lead pair, he eventually approached Naseeruddin Shah and Ratna Pathak Shah.

Vinod shared the script with Naseeruddin after star Vishal Bhardwaj helped connect them. Both Naseeruddin and Ratna liked the story and were keen to be part of the movie. However, the Main Vaapas Aaunga star had a question about whether they would be able to do justice to characters so deeply rooted in the region. “He was so candid about movie and a story and he shared you know we really wanted to do this movie and we don't want to leave this movie because this is such a beautiful script but I have one concern do you think that we belong to that place and do you think we both of us can do justice to this movie just think about it,” Vinod recalled.

title: Actors should not blame industry for typecasting, it’s their limitation: Saurabh Sachdeva
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Mumbai, Star and acting coach Saurabh Sachdeva says he does not view negative roles as mere antagonists but as individuals with distinct personalities and motivations.

Adding to this, Actors should not blame industry for typecasting, it’s their limitation: Saurabh Sachdeva Sachdeva, known for playing intense and morally complex characters in films such as "Animal", "Vadh", "Jaane Jaan" and "Dhadak 2", believes audiences may see his characters as negative but he approaches each of them differently, looking for nuances in human behaviour.

Meanwhile, "People can typecast you, but it is the shape that I have to give to the characters. If you see all my negative characters, you might say, 'Oh, it's a negative character', but they are different human beings, different personalities," Sachdeva told PTI in an interview.
Notably, "There's so much to explore in human behaviour. That's what we don't see. If we see that, then there is so much work to do for me," he added.

As per the latest buzz, Sachdeva, who currently stars in a key role in Nitesh Tiwari's "Ramayana", shared actors should not blame the industry for typecasting as he believes it is up to them to decide whether they allow themselves to be confined to a particular image.

In further updates, "If I say I've been typecast, then it's my limitation, then I'm putting myself in a box and people will see from that box. Like, you see a negative character, I see different human beings, which have their own problems, struggles and barriers, which I've to cross.

On top of that, "And those barriers should be so strong that it enhances the protagonist. Like, in 'Vadh', if the antagonist is not so strong, then the protagonist won't be able to do anything. So, I have to take it to that level."
Before foraying into acting, Sachdeva worked behind the camera as an acting coach and he attributed his delayed start as an star to personal self-doubt.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 3: Saturday surge takes Ranbir Kapoor's film past ₹375 crore, beats Adipurush, Pathaan and Animal
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

After a slower first Friday, Ramayana : Part One, starring Ranbir Kapoor , Yash and Sai Pallavi, has picked up pace at the ticket-window, with Saturday bringing a big jump in collections. The Nitesh Tiwari directorial collected its biggest single-day worldwide earnings since rollout. With its three-day worldwide gross touching ₹ 375 crore rupees, the movie has already put up some impressive numbers and is now closing in on the Day 3 record of Shah Rukh Khan's Jawan.

Adding to this, ₹375 crore rupees in 3 days! Ranbir Kapoor's movie Ramayana beats Pathaan and Animal, trails Jawan, Ramayana sees a big jump on Day 3 According to trade tracker Sacnilk, the movie had a strong Saturday, collecting ₹ 83.45 crore rupees gross in India. Overseas markets added another ₹ 60 crore rupees on the day, taking the movie's total overseas gross to ₹ 157.25 crore rupees. Its worldwide gross now stands at ₹ 375.50 crore rupees.

Meanwhile, The jump is particularly noticeable when compared to Friday's numbers. Ramayana collected ₹ 57.30 crore rupees gross in India on day 2, which means Saturday saw a 45.3% rise. The movie has also gone past its opening-day India gross of ₹ 77.50 crore rupees, making Day 3 its biggest day at the domestic ticket-window so far.

Notably, Ramayana's third-day worldwide gross has already taken it past the numbers of some major Indian films. Adipurush, which also told the tale of Ramayana starring Prabhas and Kriti Sanon, had collected ₹ 304.04 crore rupees worldwide on day 3. With that collection, Ramayana is ahead by approximately 23.5%.

As per the latest buzz, However, Jawan remains the movie to beat. Shah Rukh Khan's smash hit had collected ₹ 383.18 crore rupees worldwide on day 3 whereas Dhurandhar: The Revenge starring Ranveer Singh had surpassed over ₹ 500 crore rupees mark worldwide by the third day.

In further updates, Sunday will be an important day for Ramayana, although Diwali celebrations could affect theatre footfalls, particularly during evening and night shows. The bigger opportunity may come after the festival, when the holiday period could bring more families to theatres. Monday's collections will be worth watching, especially after the strong Saturday performance.

title: Janhvi Kapoor reveals Sridevi was unsure of her acting career, jokes her mother saw ‘potential’ in her after she got a nose job
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Janhvi Kapoor has shared an interesting memory about her late mother, Sridevi , and how she reacted to her decision to become an star. In a recent conversation with her maternal cousin, star Maheswari on Galatta Plus Tamil, Janhvi opened up that Sridevi was not entirely convinced about her entering films at first. However, she recalled a rather unexpected moment when her mother seemed to have a change of heart. According to Janhvi, it happened after she underwent a nose job.

Adding to this, Janhvi Kapoor recalls how a nose job changed Sridevi's opinion about her acting dreams: ‘Yeah, there's potential’. Sridevi had reservations about Janhvi becoming an star Looking back on the day she first told Sridevi she wanted to act, Janhvi shared her mother's unforgettable response. Sridevi gave her blessing, but not without a heavy reality check, warning Janhvi that the profession would demand everything she had. Maheswari remembered that Sridevi was not entirely convinced about Janhvi joining films, given how demanding the profession could be. “Jaanu wants to be in films, but I’m not very keen because it’s a lot of hard work, a lot of dedication, and you have to be really strong to get in there,” Maheswari recalled her saying.

Meanwhile, Janhvi then made a rather surprising revelation about what may have changed her mother's mind. Whilst laughing, she shared, “I think maybe you should cut this out, but I think before I did my nose, she was unsure. She was like, 'I don't think it's…' After I did my nose, she's like, 'Yeah, there's potential'.”

Notably, Sridevi passed away in February 2018 at the age of 54. She was in Dubai to attend the wedding celebrations of her nephew, star Mohit Marwah, when news of her sudden death emerged. The news left the movie industry and her followers in shock. title: Ramayana makers issue stern warning over leaked clips, threaten criminal action and contempt proceedings against offenders
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The makers of Ramayana : Part 1 or as it is internationally called Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, have issued a strong warning against people recording the movie inside theatres and sharing clips online. With the movie running in cinemas since November 5, the team has raised concerns over unauthorised footage being circulated on social media and messaging platforms. They have now made it clear that anyone involved in recording or distributing such content could face legal consequences. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari , the movie stars Ranbir Kapoor , Sai Pallavi and Yash in the lead roles.

Adding to this, Ramayana makers issue stern warning over leaked footage, say offenders could face criminal action. Ramayana makers cite Bombay High Court orders The movie's official social media handles shared a legal notice addressing the unauthorised recording and sharing of its footage. The makers shared they were aware of people recording portions of the movie during theatrical screenings and circulating them across various online platforms.

Meanwhile, The notice also refers to two recent Bombay High Court orders, dated November 2 and November 6, 2026, which restrict people from recording or sharing the movie without permission. It reads, “The Hon'ble Bombay High Court, by orders dated 2 November 2026 and 6 November 2026 in commercial IP suit (l) no. 37230 of 2026, has restrained all persons, known and unknown, from recording, uploading, sharing or otherwise communicating the movie or any part of it without authorisation.”

Notably, The makers have also pointed out that such actions are not limited to copyright violations and could invite criminal charges. The notice states, “Doing so is copyright infringement, a criminal offence punishable with imprisonment and fine under the Copyright Act, 1957, the Cinematograph Act, 1952, the BNS, 2023 and the IT Act, 2000, and a contempt of court.”

As per the latest buzz, Along with Sunny Deol's post-credit appearance as Lord Hanuman, which ws officially posted on the day of the rollout along with Hanuman Chalisa song, another clip from the movie has caught the attention of social media users. title: Nanncy Gill talks Udta Teer, working with Ayushmann Khurrana, directing plays and why she chose the UK over cashing in on fame
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nanncy Gill, of late seen as a Counter Terrorist Squad (CTS) agent in Ayushmann Khurrana -starrer Udta Teer , is expanding her wings with her ongoing course in the UK. She is pursuing an MA in screen and stage from the Royal Welsh College of Music and Drama in Cardiff , Wales, and is looking to take up international projects besides working in India.

Adding to this, Star Nanncy Gill and with Ayushmann Khurrana and other team members on the set of her last rollout Utda Teer. The Raisinghani vs Raisinghani (2024) star says, “After getting attention in a successful movie, the obvious thing is to cash in on the moment and look for opportunities in India, which I am getting, but I have a bigger picture in mind. I first want to complete my course and improve my craft and come with full force besides exploring opportunities here. I just wanted to expand my artistic choices.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nanncy Gill (@inanncygill)

Notably, She is looking forward to expanding in India and abroad. "I don't just want to be a screen star. I really love theatre also and I want to be a complete artist. In the direction of my career, I want to be an star, writer and theatre director, building my career in the UK as well."

As per the latest buzz, Gill got this confidence by dabbling deeply in theatre. "I'm not only limited to being an star now. I wrote, produced and directed my own theatre plays and that gave me a different viewpoint. So, I want to build an international career and this is the right time for me. Leaving India at a high point of my career was tough but I had to make a hard choice."

In further updates, Back in India, she directed two plays, House Arrest and Mandi House . “After Mumbai, we did Delhi's Shri Ram Center and people really loved it. I have started getting opportunities here. I shot for a BBC short movie two weeks back for experience. Besides, I have written a play, which I have submitted to my college and if they approve it, I'm going to get all the production to do a ticketed play. Once that happens, I can develop my own. In the UK, theatre is big, so opportunities are there where I can bring my Indian roots into play!”

On top of that, Playing CTS agent Sharon, she was part of the team with Ayushmann. "Shooting with him was really great as he is a very humble person and he makes everyone so comfortable. We shot for 45 days in Manali. Of course, some of my scenes and dialogues were cut but the makers are the best judge. But having a presence throughout the movie is a big deal and a great experience. It's humbling to see people posting stories and appreciation coming my way. After the OTT rollout, the visibility will be more."

She recalls being in Dubai when she got the call. “Besides my audition, they wanted to see my fitness and action videos. I put them together with my gym, kalaripayattu, boxing and MMA ones and sent them. I got selected and then came to know what project it was for. We did lots of tough action sequences under Korean action director Oh Se-Yeong and it was great fun. Interestingly, I watched it in London, in a theatre, and people were like, 'Hey, you're in the movie.' It felt nice.”

title: Amitabh Bachchan wins personality rights case; Delhi High Court passes final decree after four defendants settle
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Court held that the right to control the commercial use of an individual's identity falls under the “right to publicity”. It observed that Bachchan's name and photographs had been used without permission in ways that could falsely suggest his endorsement of products or services.

Adding to this, The star had approached the Court over the alleged unauthorised use of his identity across different platforms and merchandise. These included a mobile application titled Amitabh Bachchan Video Call, messages promoting a purported Kaun Banega Crorepati lottery, a general knowledge quiz book featuring his photograph, T-shirts, posters and domain names incorporating his identity.
Meanwhile, The Court noted that the unauthorised use involved Bachchan's “very name and photographs” and found that the requirements for protecting his publicity rights had been met.

Notably, The final decree also covers unidentified individuals, commonly referred to as John Does. The Court took note of the continued use of Bachchan's persona through anonymous websites, applications, posters and messaging platforms, observing that those responsible may not always be identifiable.

As per the latest buzz, Four defendants, Rajat Nagi, Manoj Publications, Tamatina and Mahesh Patel, settled the matter with Bachchan and acknowledged his publicity and privacy rights. As part of the settlement, the defendants agreed to discontinue the use of his identity. The commitments included deleting the video-call application, stopping publication of the quiz book and sale of posters, and deleting the domain name amitabhbachchan.in.

In further updates, The remaining defendants did not appear before the Court or file written statements despite being served. The Court held that the case did not involve disputed facts requiring a trial and granted a summary judgment against them. It also clarified that Bachchan could initiate fresh proceedings if further unauthorised use of his persona occurs.
On top of that, The November 2022 interim injunction now stands merged with the final decree.

title: Dhanush says no one other than Sai Pallavi could have played Sita in Ramayana, calls her a great performer
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The star was speaking at a pre-rollout event of the movie, where he shared how he does not understand the chatter around the casting of Sai as Sita in Ramayana. Dhanush shared that even if there was a search in whole of India for the role of Sita, no one could have done justice to the part other than Sai Pallavi.

Adding to this, Sai Pallavi at the premiere of Ramayana at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello) (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello) What Dhanush shared Dhanush spoke about Sai on stage and shared how they first worked together in Maari 2, when she was extremely shy off camera and a person with few words. After nine years when the two of them worked again in OM, Dhanush shared that he was surprised at the complete transformation of Sai. “She stood there as if she totally mastered the art of cinema. title: Pyre director Vinod Kapri says 75% shows of film has been cut down within first week, reveals theatre owners were told only one film will be shown
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

National Award-winning fimmaker Vinod Kapri’s Pyre rolled out in theatres last week to rave reviews. The movie tells the story of an elderly couple who continue to wait for their children, even as life in their Himalayan village grows quieter with each passing day. On Saturday, the filmmaker took to X to share that majority of the shows of the movie has been removed for a bigger movie to rollout and theatre owners were told that only one movie will play now.

Adding to this, Vinod Kapri's Hindi movie Pyre rolled out in theatres across India on October 30 ‘This is not fair’ In a video post, the filmmaker shared that he did not want to make this video statement because of the need of the hour. He shared that Pyre had a limited rollout from the beginning, in around 80 screens. But because of the love that the movie got, the number extended to 400. But, since the last two days, 75% of the shows have been cut of Pyre and now the number is less than 100.

Meanwhile, “We are in touch with theatre owners and distributors. They have been told that no other movie will be running in theatres except one movie. I do not understand why you have to run your movie by stopping other films? Is this a win of good over evil? Is there any honor in doing this? The honor with which we tell a story. This is a small movie, with non actors, and people are crying after seeing it. What honor, truth and goodness do you boast when this is the way theatres are ordered? I urge theatre owners and distributors to not do this with Pyre. If you have spent a lot of money, then we have spent our soul in making a movie. We deserve a fair chance,” he shared.

Notably, “This is not fair, not to Pyre. Not to your audience,” read the caption of the post. Although Vinod did not name the big movie in question, the big rollout over the last two days is Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash in lead roles. title: Ramayana box office collection day 3: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi film sees growth on Saturday, crosses ₹182 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana rolled out in theatres on November 5. The movie did great business on its opening day, setting a new record for a pre-Diwali rollout in India. However, the collections hit a dip on the second day, given it was a non-holiday and right before the weekend. The movie is expected to pick up pace on Saturday ahead of Diwali and recover during the weekend. It remains to be seen how Ramayana fares in its first weekend, so let us take a detailed look at the ticket-window performance so far.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor is portraying Lord Rama in the movie Ramayana. Ramayana ticket-window update Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 days before rollout. By the time of its rollout, the movie had already sold tickets worth ₹ 200 crore rupees worldwide. The movie went on to collect ₹ 64.85 crore rupees in India on its first day of rollout, becoming the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. Friday saw a dip, and the movie collected only ₹ 48.05 crore rupees. Despite Yash ’s presence as Ravana, the Kannada version has started extremely slowly. On Saturday though, the occupancy rate of the Kannada version improved.

Meanwhile, By 10 PM on day 3, the movie had collected ₹ 69.80 crore rupees net in India, taking its three-day haul to ₹ 182.70 crore rupees , according to the trade website Sacnilk. This shows that the movie has managed to show a significant improvement on Saturday. The movie is now eyeing the ₹ 200 crore rupees mark, which it is expected to cross by Sunday.

Notably, By the end of day 3, Adipurush had collected above ₹ 200 crore rupees net in India. It remains to be seen whether Ramayana can cross that mark. However, it must be noted that Adipurush’s first three days in theatres were a Friday, Saturday and Sunday, while Ramayana’s first three days included a working Thursday and Friday, and then Saturday. However, Ramayana has managed to beat the opening-day hauls of blockbusters such as Pathaan ( ₹ 57 crore rupees), Animal ( ₹ 63 crore rupees), and Drishyam 2 ( ₹ 62 crore rupees).

title: Farah Khan says the film industry makes people insecure about themselves, admits she felt the same before making her first film Main Hoon Na
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Farah Khan has worn many hats in her decades-long career as a choreographer, filmmaker, show judge, and now, a YouTuber. In a recent chat with Neha Dhupia, Angad Bedi on their podcast, Farah was asked about her recent hit YouTube channel, in which she visits the houses of her star friends with her cook Dilip. Farah shared that she did not plan of continuing her channel for so long but it has been a welcome change in her lifestyle.

Adding to this, Farah Khan shared why she started her YouTube channel. What Farah shared When Neha congratulated Farah on her YouTube channel and asked that now that it has crossed 300 episodes and become such a big hit, did she plan this from the beginning? Farah denied any planning for the YouTube channel and shared that she had some free time after finishing her script for her next movie and started her YouTube journey to not feel angsty in that period. She shared, “Later everyone shared that I pivoted at the right time but that is all destiny. I get angsty and if one is not doing anything then after waking up they think that my movie is not hapenning and someone else is making theirs. I can't go through that. I have been through it when I wanted to make my first movie.”

Meanwhile, “This industry makes you insecure. Because at all times you are comparing yourself to somebody else. That this star is doing this movie and what not. When I hit 50, I told myself that I want to detach, cut off and live a happy life. But ofcourse, we are hustlers and YouTube is something that I didn't realise that there was a lack of family-oriented content perhaps and people liked it and ofcourse they liked Dilip. As we went along, we kept tweaking the format,” she added.

Notably, Farah Khan's YouTube channel currently has over 3 million followers. In her vlogs, Farah visits the homes of celebrities to cook new dishes with them in their kitchens, gives viewers a tour of their homes, and indulges in fun conversations over food. Her quirky banter with her cook Dilip has become the highlight of the videos, helping him rise to social media fame. In one of the vlogs, the filmmaker also admitted to having increased Dilip’s salary since they began their YouTube journey.

As per the latest buzz, Farah made her directorial debut with Main Hoon Na in 2004. It starred Shah Rukh Khan and Sushmita Sen. She then directed Om Shanti Om with Shah Rukh Khan, and Tees Maar Khan with Akshay Kumar. Her last directorial was Happy New Year, which rolled out in 2014.

title: Vivek Oberoi recalls being ostracised from Bollywood for standing up against what he perceived as wrong; says filmmakers got calls from underworld
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Vivek Oberoi was considered one of the rising stars in the early 2000s thanks to films like Company and Saathiya. However, one press conference in 2003 seemed to change it all for him. Now, years later, Vivek claimed on the Relearn podcast that he was ‘in hell’ during the fallout of the row. He also claimed that filmmakers who wanted to work with him would get calls from the underworld, warning them against it.

Adding to this, Vivek Oberoi most of late starred in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. (AFP) Vivek Oberoi recalls being ostracised from Bollywood Vivek was asked to talk about the row he faced in the early 2000s even as his career was taking off. Without taking names or getting into details of what happened, he shared, “It was a very dark phase in my life. I tried to stand up for something. I came from the thought process that there’s a certain line you don’t cross. Women have to be respected and treated a certain way. I stood up to what I perceived was wrong, and I started being bullied a lot. Despite delivering successes, hits, and awards, a very powerful lobby took over. I became persona non grata. I would have people pulling out of films I had signed.”

Meanwhile, He also claimed that everything ‘snowballed and just got worse’ for him, with filmmakers dropping him from projects. And those who stood by him would allegedly receive calls from the underworld. “Those who decided to stick by me for ethical reasons would suddenly call me a few weeks later and say, listen man, I got a call from the underworld. I had gangsters calling me, saying that, you movie with this guy and you’re done; you’re toast. I went through real hell, real misery. I didn’t get the work not because I wasn’t able to deliver. It wasn’t based on talent. It wasn’t based on performance. It wasn’t based on work ethic. It was based on something that I couldn’t control,” shared Vivek.

Notably, Vivek experienced career fluctuations after early success. He even tried to play morally grey and dark characters in films such as Krrish 3, Vivegam, and Lucifer. After starring in Kesari Veer and Masti 4 in 2025, he starred in Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana Part 1 this year. The star played Ravana’s brother-in-law and Surpanaka’s husband, Vidyutjihva, in the movie. He now has Sandeep Reddy Vanga’s Spirit lined up for rollout. The movie stars Prabhas and Triptii Dimri in lead roles. It will be rolled out next year.

title: Ranbir Kapoor reveals plans for directorial debut, says he wants to move behind the camera in 2-3 years: ‘It's my last decade as an actor’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ranbir Kapoor has started working on a script for his directorial debut. The star, who is currently seen as Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana : Part 1, spoke about his plans to move behind the camera during an interview with co-star Sai Pallavi for BBC Asian News Network. While he hasn't decided on all the details of his first movie, Ranbir knows the kind of story he wants to tell. He is hoping to begin shooting it in the next two or three years, once he has wrapped up his current acting projects.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor says he is 'dying to direct a movie', reveals plans to make his first movie in 2-3 years. (PTI) Ranbir Kapoor on writing his first movie Ranbir opened up that he started working on a script a few months ago, but the experience has been far more challenging than he expected. Writing has given him a new respect for the people who create stories and bring them to life on screen. He also spoke about the satisfaction of being a director and having the opportunity to bring different people together to tell a story.

Meanwhile, Explaining what appeals to him about the craft, he shared, “I just started writing a script a couple of months back, and it’s so hard to create. I have so much respect for writers and creators. ‘How do you create?’ It’s exciting because I truly believe that after a musician, if there’s somebody who feels a creative high, it’s the director. An star’s high is very superficial but the director, when he directs a movie, however good or bad, the opportunity to tell a story and get all these people together to tell your story, it’s just a beautiful experience and I hope I can do it.”

Notably, Ranbir is still figuring out what his first movie as a director will look like, but he has a fair idea of the kind of stories he wants to tell. He mentioned Life is Beautiful, It's a Wonderful Life and Rajkumar Hirani's films among his favourites, and shared he would like to make a family drama that leaves people with a warm, feel-good experience.

As per the latest buzz, He also explained how he hopes to balance direction with his acting career. Ranbir shared he usually works for around 100 to 125 days a year, leaving him time to write and develop ideas. Sharing his plans, he shared, “I work only 100-125 days a year; I have a lot of time to write stories. I’ve never ever been so busy, never ever been so committed. I’ve always had one movie out, and then I would start working on the other movie. But, I guess, it’s my last decade as an star; will I get to play these parts? I do want to kind of pivot towards direction. I don’t want to direct myself for sure. I really want to get these films done (Brahmastra 2, Animal 2 and Ramayana Part 2), and really get on floors with my directorial debut within 2 or 3 years, I hope.”

In further updates, After Ramayana: Part One, Ranbir will be starring in Love & War . The Sanjay Leela Bhansali directorial also features Alia Bhatt and Vicky Kaushal and is set to rollout on January 21, 2027. The star also has Animal Park, helmed by Sandeep Reddy Vanga and then Ramayana: Part Two for 2028.

title: Exclusive| Hansal Mehta on Ranveer Singh starrer Pralay row: Mumbai, the home of Indian cinema has become most unfriendly to shoot in
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Hansal Mehta has responded to the row over the shoot of R anveer Singh -starrer Pralay at Mumbai’s Azad Maidan, saying the team had secured the required permissions. The row began after the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) raised objections to the six-hour shoot, claiming it forced the postponement of inter-school cricket matches. The association has questioned why a ground used by young cricketers was made available for a commercial movie shoot.

Adding to this, Hansal Mehta, Ranveer Singh In conversation with us Mehta says, “Our shoot at Azad Maidan was fully permitted. We have requisite permission letters from police departments, sports departments including an acknowledgement of the same from MCA. The larger problem is this. Mumbai is the home of Indian cinema. It has also become a most unfriendly city to shoot in. A single location needs clearances from multiple departments, each with its own process, its own delays and its own power to stop a shoot. Even when you have every permission, you are treated as if you are trespassing.”

Meanwhile, He adds that so many other states welcome movie crews. He says, “They understand that a shoot brings jobs, business and visibility. Here, we are met with obstruction. I say this with much sadness as a proud Mumbaikar and Maharashtrian - This is why so many of us now prefer to shoot outside Mumbai.”

Notably, However he continues saying he wants to shoot in Mumbai. “I have worked in this city for over three decades. I love it and I want to keep telling its stories here. But filmmakers will go where they are allowed to work. If Mumbai wants to remain the centre of this industry, it has to stop treating its own filmmakers as a nuisance.We followed every rule no matter how complicated or difficult it may be. We will continue to do so. We simply seek the cooperation of the authorities and a much needed lack of mistrust in doing so.”

title: Arunachal govt releases 4 Siang dam protesters, seeks fresh dialogue
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Arunachal Pradesh government on Saturday rolled out four protesters detained during the agitation against the proposed 1,000-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), signalling an attempt to end the prolonged standoff with organisations opposing the project.

Adding to this, A formal response from SIFF is awaited. (HT Sourced Photo) The four protesters — Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron — were detained under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014, following protests in the Siang Valley.

Meanwhile, Their rollout came a day after the chief minister’s office (CMO), in a letter dated November 6, informed the Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum (SIFF) of the government’s decision to free the detainees as a goodwill gesture aimed at creating an atmosphere conducive to dialogue and reconciliation.
Notably, The government also approved the reinstatement of gaon buras and gaon buris (traditional village authorities) who faced disciplinary action in connection with the agitation.

As per the latest buzz, These decisions address two of the major concerns raised by SIFF, which had earlier refused to engage in talks with Chief Minister Pema Khandu until its demands were fulfilled.

On top of that, Responding to SIFF’s demand for the immediate withdrawal of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel, the government maintained that decisions regarding security deployment must be guided by law-and-order considerations and public safety.

title: Nitesh Tiwari says he believes Homer was inspired by Ramayana for The Odyssey; Ranbir Kapoor calls bow-lifting scene coincidence
body: Here's the latest update from the Hollywood/Marvel world:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana hit screens on November 5. But much before that, Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey had followers pumped for it purely because of a scene involving a queen choosing her groom and a bow and arrow. Nitesh and Ranbir Kapoor , who plays Lord Rama, of late discussed the parallels between the Indian epic and Homer’s Odyssey.

Adding to this, Queen Penelope and Sita both ask suitors and lift and string a complicated bow in The Odyssey and Ramayana. Nitesh Tiwari, Ranbir Kapoor on The Odyssey, Ramayana Talking to Screen Rant , Nitesh shared that he believed Homer might have been inspired by the Ramayana, given the parallels in the stories. “Ramayana is the oldest epic, and I believe Homer was inspired by Ramayana in some way; having written those bits in Odyssey. And yes, I did notice those equivalents and I felt very happy that our greatest epic has got a tribute in another epic which belongs to the West side, and it's going to make it very easier for the people to also connect with what we were trying to bring to the West also,” he shared.

Meanwhile, Ranbir pointed out that the Ramayana was written thousands of years ago, but called the parallels a sweet coincidence, particularly in the bow-lifting scene. “To be honest, it's written in our text 4,000 years ago. So actually, when I saw Odyssey, I thought, 'That's from Ramayana.' Exactly. But yeah, sweet coincidence. I love The Odyssey . I love Christopher Nolan. But yeah, doing Ramayana had a very different feeling,” shared the star. He also shared that he had ‘goosebumps’ while performing the scene, and could feel a ‘weird current going up and down’ when he lifted the bow.

Notably, During the climax of The Odyssey, Odysseus (Matt Damon) has been away for too long and presumed dead. Penelope (Anne Hathaway) is willing to finally select a suitor, but only if they pass the test she has set for them. The suitors must not just string a bow that only her husband has been able to, but they must also fire an arrow through 12 axe heads to win her in marriage.

As per the latest buzz, While this scene is a setup for something far more than it seems on the surface, it was hard for the Indian audience not to draw parallels to Sita's swayamvar. In Ramayana, suitors are called to Mithila by King Janaka to seek his daughter Sita’s hand in marriage. Suitors must be able to lift a bow called Shivadhanush, which only she has managed to lift so far. Rama not only lifts it, but he also breaks it by mistake while stringing it. Sai Pallavi plays Sita, and Yash plays Ravana in Ramayana.

In further updates, Despite having a Master's degree in Journalism and over a decade of experience in print and digital media as a field reporter and sub-editor at organisations such as The Times of India and Reader's Digest, Neeshita Nyayapati remains a movie buff first and a Chief Content Producer second. She fell in love with movies in childhood and believes nothing matches the magic of watching a good movie that moves you with a warm tub of popcorn in hand. Her love for writing about cinema follows that. Come Friday, you'll find her at her happy place, the movies, catching the latest rom-com or masala offering, for reviews or otherwise. As for the rest of the week, she's here reporting the juiciest news in Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada and Hindi or bringing out the best of celebs in interviews. While her niche is Telugu cinema, Neeshita likes to dabble in a little bit of everything to stay up to date. From movie announcements to scandals and hard news angles, she has explored it all. A good book, a comforting cup of hot chocolate, puppy kisses and a stunning beach view are all she needs to unwind. Her passion for biking and travelling has taken her to various places across the country. She has found peace in everything from the frozen lakes of Gangtok to the coffee plantations of Coorg and the dense forests of Bandipur, to the monasteries of Darjeeling. title: How far should films go in depicting violence? Experts weigh in on its impact on kids
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
“There are a few emotions that are very easy to provoke the audience with. Violence is one of them, and sex is another.”

Adding to this, Recent cases of children and young adults involved in violent incidents reignited debate over violence in films. This observation by Aamir Khan in an old interview resurfaced on social media when Sandeep Reddy Vanga's Animal was rolled out in 2023. Among the many aspects of the movie that sparked debate, its graphic violence became a major talking point online. However, Animal was far from the only movie to face criticism over its portrayal of violence. Over the past five years, several blockbusters across movie industries have been called out on social media for not just depicting extreme violence but also seemingly glorifying it on the big screen. The Dhurandhar duology, which emerged as the highest-grossing Indian films of 2025 and 2026, is among the latest and biggest examples.
Meanwhile, Violence in cinema has always been a subject of debate, but the two recent troubling real-life instances have once again brought the conversation into focus.

Notably, In Haryana's Panchkula, an eight-year-old boy allegedly assaulted a six-year-old girl inside a school classroom, repeatedly hitting her with an object that appeared to be a brick. In another disturbing incident in Andhra Pradesh, a 21-year-old allegedly entered a Class 10 classroom carrying a chainsaw and attacked a girl student, leaving two injured.

As per the latest buzz, While there is no direct link between these incidents and what we see in films, the graphic nature of these cases has once again raised questions about how far filmmakers should go when depicting violence on screen. For instance, in Dhurandhar, Akshaye Khanna's character, Rehman Dakait, is seen smashing a man's face. In Animal, Ranbir Kapoor's character enters a college classroom carrying a rifle to intimidate students.

In further updates, The debate is not limited to Hindi cinema. When Rajinikanth's Jailer was rolled out in 2023, its graphic sequences, including scenes involving torture and acid, drew criticism from some viewers. Similarly, Allu Arjun's smash hit Pushpa 2: The Rule, the highest-grossing Indian movie of 2024, drew criticism for its graphic climax sequences, with some viewers finding the brutality on screen hard to digest.

On top of that, With screens becoming an increasingly unavoidable part of children's lives, monitoring the content they consume has become important. Experts point out that younger children may not always have the ability to distinguish between fiction and reality and, hence, they can’t fully understand the consequences of imitating what they see on screen.

Dr Subhrajit Parida, consultant, paediatrics and neonatology, Manipal Hospital, Bhubaneswar, explains that children can imitate the behaviour of characters they admire, particularly heroes who are often rewarded for their violent actions.

title: Delhi High Court rules Doosra infringed Sourav Ganguly's personality rights, directs makers to deposit Rs. 2 crores
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The ruling comes in connection with a lawsuit filed by Sourav Ganguly along with Luv Films over the unauthorised use of his identity and life events in the movie. The Court has also restrained the makers from releasing Doosra on OTT platforms or through any other medium.

Adding to this, According to the Court's observations, elements of Ganguly's personality and incidents from his life are closely connected to the movie's narrative. This makes it difficult to remove the portions in question from the final cut. The Court, therefore, directed the makers to include prominent disclaimers to clarify the nature of the movie's association with the former cricketer.

Meanwhile, The disclaimers must explicitly state that Ganguly did not give consent for the commercial use or depiction of his persona in the movie. They must also clarify that the project does not have any official association or authorisation from him.

Notably, The ruling brings attention to the legal issues surrounding the use of public figures' identities and personal histories in films and other commercial projects. Personality rights generally protect individuals against the unauthorised commercial exploitation of aspects such as their name, image and likeness.

title: Hansal Mehta denies cricket body's claims of match disruptions over Ranveer Singh's Pralay shoot in Mumbai, says team had Azad Maidan clearance
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Hansal Mehta has responded to the row over the shoot of Ranveer Singh-starrer Pralay at Mumbai's Azad Maidan, saying the team had secured the required permissions. The row began after the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) raised objections to the six-hour shoot, claiming it forced the postponement of inter-school cricket matches. The association has questioned why a ground used by young cricketers was made available for a commercial movie shoot.

Adding to this, Pralay shoot row: Hansal Mehta rejects MCA's claims, says team had permission to movie at Azad Maidan. Hansal, meanwhile, maintained that the production had secured all the required permissions before filming at Azad Maidan. In conversation with Mumbai Mirror, he also criticised the hurdles filmmakers face while shooting in Mumbai, saying, “But I would like to underscore that Mumbai has been rendered a no-go zone for movie shoots because of bureaucratic hurdles. And people like you fuel the fire.”

Meanwhile, The MCA shared it had written to the Maharashtra government's Sports Department, seeking an explanation for allowing the Pralay shoot at Azad Maidan. As per the report, the association shared it was not consulted before the permission was issued, even though it is responsible for maintaining the ground and its pitches. The shoot required a large set to be put up and artificial grass to be laid, which left the MCA with no choice but to reschedule Under-14 and Under-16 inter-school matches already on the calendar.

Notably, MCA Apex Council member Nadim Memon shared Azad Maidan was already losing space to activities unrelated to sport. A section of the ground had been taken over for the Aqua Line Metro work, but the contractors had not moved out despite repeated reminders. The Mumbai Police also continued to occupy the premises instead of returning to their original location. He questioned why a movie shoot was now being allowed when the ground was already dealing with these issues. He accused the Sports Department of giving commercial bookings priority over the needs of young sportspersons and shared its decisions were affecting the cricketing culture that Azad Maidan has supported for years.

As per the latest buzz, Nadim shared this was the first time a movie had been shot at the ground and questioned the disruption caused to players and ongoing tournaments. He shared, “This is the first time a movie shoot has taken place at Azad Maidan. Large sets were erected, and artificial grass was laid for the shoot of Pralay. This is not a movie-shooting venue but a cricket ground where players hone their skills to progress to the international level. Our ongoing tournaments were disrupted because of the shoot. Who will take responsibility for this loss? You cannot commercially exploit a cricket ground by allowing a commercial movie shoot.”

In further updates, The report shared that the Maharashtra government had allowed Light Rays, the production house behind Pralay, to use 5,000 square yards of Azad Maidan for a six-hour shoot. The company paid ₹ 40,000 for the booking and deposited another ₹ 40,000 as security, which is refundable. The permission was signed by Sports Department Under Secretary Ashok Damayyawar on October 30 and sent on November 2. It came with conditions, including no vehicles on the pitches and no cooking or digging on the ground. The production was also required to obtain an NOC from the MCA. The association, however, says it was not consulted before the department approved the shoot.

On top of that, Deputy Director of Sports, Mumbai Division, Navnath Fartade, defended the decision, saying a government resolution allows Azad Maidan to host non-sporting events for up to 30 days in a year. The MCA is concerned that allowing commercial shoots at the ground could lead to more such bookings and leave even less room for cricket. Azad Maidan regularly hosts inter-school and age-group tournaments, coaching sessions and club matches. The association wants the Sports Department to prioritise these activities and ensure that young players do not lose access to the ground due to commercial events.

Ranveer Singh is leading the movie Pralay, a survival thriller set in a post-catastrophic Mumbai. Set in a post-apocalyptic world, the movie follows the zombie threat as people struggle to survive in a city pushed to the edge. Directed by Jai Mehta, the movie is being mounted on a large scale for a theatrical rollout.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 2: Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash film overtakes Adipurush with ₹221 crore haul
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana Part 1 was rolled out in theatres on November 5, receiving mixed reviews and decent box-office numbers. The movie, which had a lower opening than Om Raut’s Prabhas, Kriti Sanon, and Saif Ali Khan-starrer Adipurush, seemed to recover on its second day. The Ranbir Kapoor , Sai Pallavi, and Yash-starrer has now overtaken the previous Ramayana adaptation.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor and Yash play Rama and Ravana in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window earnings Ramayana grossed ₹ 127.50 crore rupees on its opening day, compared to Adipurush's ₹ 128 crore rupees, despite the latter not having as wide an opening as the Nitesh movie. While the movie saw a dip in collections in India on its second day, bringing in ₹ 48.05 crore rupees net versus the ₹ 64.85 crore rupees opening, the movie managed to outpace Adipurush in worldwide collections.

Meanwhile, Ramayana collected ₹ 35 crore rupees from overseas on its second day, taking its overseas gross to ₹ 86.25 crore rupees, according to the trade website Sacnilk. Adding to that, the ₹ 134.80 crore rupees gross collection from India in two days takes its two-day worldwide haul to ₹ 221.05 crore rupees. Adipurush had grossed ₹ 215.78 crore rupees worldwide in two days. Ramayana, however, had a much wider rollout than Adipurush , with 23,316 shows in India alone, compared to 16,120 for the latter movie.

Notably, Compared to other juggernauts, despite the difference in genre, Ramayana is lagging behind Aditya Dhar’s Dhurandhar: The Revenge. The Ranveer Singh-starrer had grossed ₹ 358.86 crore rupees in two days. It is also behind Ranbir’s previous movie, Animal, with Sandeep Reddy Vanga, which grossed ₹ 236.01 crore rupees in two days. But with the movie now entering its first weekend, and Sunday being Diwali, it remains to be seen how much it collects before facing a weekday slump.

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana is directed by Nitesh Tiwari , who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. It is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash. Ranbir plays Ram, Sai plays Sita, and Yash plays Ravana in this adaptation of the Indian epic. It also stars Ravi Dubey, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan, and Lara Dutta in key roles.

title: Salman Khan explains dichotomy of having love song like Teri Sexy Beauty in war film like Maatrubhumi
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Salman Khan and Chitrangada Singh at the trailer launch of their soon-to-release movie Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace. (PTI) Salman Khan on Teri Sexy Beauty in Maatrubhumi Salman acknowledged that many must be wondering how a song like Teri Sexy Beauty fits in a movie such as Maatrubhumi. “I know everyone’s wondering how Teri Sexy Beauty fits into Maatrubhumi. Isn’t it on everyone’s mind? You will understand how it fits when you watch the movie. It comes on when an officer and several soldiers praise their wives. Whatever songs we’ve shown you, those visuals will be quite few in the movie,” he explained.

Adding to this, He also joked about how Maatrubhumi has been on a promotional run for a while now, adding, “I know you feel like we have rolled out 1400 songs, but there’s a reason for it. I’m sure you all know it. We will clear it all up today. We could not show the situations in the movie beforehand. When you watch the movie, you’ll understand how they all fit in. We can’t reveal the situation behind them all now.”

Meanwhile, Salman also humorously added that the makers did not want to give the audience a chance to take breaks through the movie, saying, “Usually, when you see music channels playing the whole song, and then you watch the movie, you feel like you’ve already seen it. You want to take a bathroom or cigarette break then. We don’t want to give you that chance; control and sit through the movie.”

title: Farah Khan admits film industry insiders were unsure of Shreya Ghoshal for Main Hoon Na songs
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Singer Shreya Ghoshal has sung some of the most melodious songs in Bollywood over the last two decades. The singer won her first National Award as a playback singer for her debut with Devdas itself, at a very young age. Filmmaker and YouTuber Farah Khan visited Shreya's Mumbai residence for her latest vlog, where they chatted about their long correspondence, which began with the rollout of Main Hoon Na. The 2004 rollout also included songs sung by Shreya.

Adding to this, Farah Khan and Shreya Ghoshal recalled memories of the making of Main Hoon Na. Farah recalls how many doubted Shreya But at the time the songs were being recorded for the Shah Rukh Khan-starrer, Shreya was a brand-newcomer, and her songs from Devdas weren't rolled out. Farah and Shreya recalled memories from that time during their conversation. Farah opened up that several people from the movie industry had even told her not to work with such a young singer, questioning her ability to pull off the songs. But Farah, as well as music composer Anu Malik, firmly believed in Shreya’s talent and went ahead with her.

Meanwhile, Shreya shared, “When I saw Sushmita on screen… how beautiful she looked, and I was wondering whether I had done justice to the songs.” Farah added, “You sang Main Hoon Na (title track) also very well, that little portion for Amrita Rao… and after hearing that, we gave you the Sushmita track in the movie. So many people called me and asked why I was taking this new girl, that I was making a big mistake! But I shared that I wanted a fresh voice.”
Notably, Shreya Ghoshal sang two tracks for the 2004 Bollywood movie Main Hoon Na, composed by Anu Malik with lyrics by Javed Akhtar. They were the title track, and the song Tumhe Jo Maine Dekha.

As per the latest buzz, Main Hoon Na, rolled out in 2004, marked Farah Khan’s directorial debut and starred Shah Rukh Khan, Sushmita Sen, Suniel Shetty, Amrita Rao and Zayed Khan. The movie follows Major Ram, who goes undercover as a college student while working on a military mission. Alongside its action and romance, the movie also focuses on family relationships and Ram’s bond with his half-brother Lakshman. It became a commercial success and remains one of the popular Hindi films of the 2000s.

body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

CJP protest live updates: The Kochi march will be CJP's first major protest since some of its leaders were arrested in Delhi last month while attempting to hold a demonstration at Jantar Mantar. CJP protest live updates: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will hold a protest march in Kerala's Kochi today, demanding the withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Titled “Jantar Mantar at Kochi”, the demonstration will take place at Rajendra Maidan from 4 pm, the group shared in a post on X. ...Read More

Adding to this, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and star-activist Prakash Raj are among those scheduled to attend. The stir will also be joined by CJP national leader Afreen Nawaz and its South India in-charge Vijay Reddy Mallangi. CJP's first major protest after Delhi crackdown The Kochi march will be CJP's first major protest since some of its leaders were arrested in Delhi last month while attempting to hold a demonstration at Jantar Mantar against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the SIR exercise. CJP co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested after entering Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The Delhi Police had denotified the site as a designated protest venue last month. Dipke was later detained ahead of a Tiranga March revealed by the party in Delhi. The Delhi Police crime branch also of late questioned CJP leaders in connection with cases linked to protests in the national capital. BJP vs CJP over ‘foreign funding’ Union minister Jitendra Singh launched an attack on the CJP earlier this week, alleging that activists were receiving funds from anti-India organisations operating within and outside the country. In conversation with the media in Bengaluru, Singh claimed there was sufficient evidence to show that Dipke was receiving funds from unauthorised sources. CJP leaders responded by asking Singh, “Why were you negotiating with us then?” They were referring to meetings between group leaders and Singh, along with Union minister JP Nadda, during the CJP's protest against the government over the NEET issue earlier this year. Ranka asked, "Why were you negotiating with us then?" Saurav Das hit back at the minister, calling the allegation “baseless”. title: Hanuman Ansh OTT release: After its ₹342 crore box office run, devotional film based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba to arrive on SonyLIV
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Hanuman Ansh , the sensational movie about the life of Neem Karoli Baba, is finally coming to OTT. On Friday, director Vishal Chaturvedi revealed via a joint Instagram post that Hanuman Ansh will stream on SonyLIV from November 27! The devotional movie, made with a shoestring budget and no stars, has emerged as one of the biggest ticket-window success stories in Indian cinema history. The movie crossed the ₹ 300 crore rupees mark at the domestic ticket-window, a staggering feat given the movie was mounted on a mere ₹ 2 crore rupees budget.

Adding to this, Shobhinaw Satyaa plays the titular role in Hanuman Ansh. When and where to watch The announcement for the OTT rollout of Hanuman Ansh read, "A divine force. An extraordinary story. A movie loved by the nation, now coming home. Hanuman Ansh, arriving on Sony LIV on 27th November!"
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sony LIV (@sonylivindia)

Notably, Hanuman Ansh tells the story of Lakshminarayan, a young man who loses his mother and begins searching for answers about God, life and death. His search takes him across North India, where he tries to make sense of human suffering and the larger questions of existence. This spiritual journey eventually leads to his transformation into Neem Karoli Baba, whose teachings continue to inspire devotees around the world.
As per the latest buzz, The movie stars Shobhinaw Satyaa in the lead role alongside Vihaan Shedge, Chandan K Anand, Purnima Tiwari, Anil Rastogi, Gulshan Pandey and Bhagvandas Patel.

In further updates, The movie collected ₹ 342.44 crore rupees net and ₹ 452.86 crore rupees worldwide, according to figures shared by Sacnilk. The movie had a slow start and was actually written off after its first two weeks in theatres. Hanuman Ansh opened at a paltry ₹ 10 lakh and had collected barely ₹ 1.50 crore rupees in its first two weeks. However, after that, positive word of mouth took over, and the ticket sales shot up. Since its fourth week, Hanuman Ansh collected over ₹ 60 crore rupees in net at the Indian ticket-window each week. In its eighth week, Hanuman Ansh crossed the ₹ 300-crore rupees mark at the domestic ticket-window, something fewer than 25 Hindi films have managed before it. It spent over 80 days at the ticket-window, a momentous feat in itself.

On top of that, Hanuman Ansh managed to surpass the lifetime ticket-window hauls of several pan-India films, including Vijay’s Jana Nayagan ( ₹ 324 crore rupees), Yash’s Toxic ( ₹ 341 crore rupees) and Ram Charan’s Peddi ( ₹ 342 crore rupees).

title: Amitabh Bachchan’s Juhu bungalow Jalsa among locations named in bomb threat email: Report
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The threat comes amid heightened security around the star following an earlier alert and the recent firing incident involving Tiger Shroff in Juhu.
Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan’s bungalow named in bomb threat email

Following the threat, security personnel immediately initiated searches at the premises identified in the email.
